programmes.name: Solo Founders Program (SFP)
programmes.organisation: Solo Founders / ODF (nZero Labs, Julian Weisser)
programmes.page_evidence: Page reads: 'A three-month program in SF for solo founders. $100K investment.' and 'Apply by Sept 2026'.
programmes.cohort_dates: Three months in San Francisco; cohort 4 (Fall 2026). Exact start date not stated on the page.
programmes.cash: $100,000 investment
programmes.terms_dilution: Search results describe MFN uncapped SAFE with 2.5% equity to participate; the programme page itself only says '$100K investment on founder-friendly terms'. The 2.5% figure is NOT from the programme page and needs verification.
programmes.network_quality: Small and highly specific: the only programme found in this sweep built exclusively around solo founding. Alumni named on the page include Supermemory (raised $3M during the programme, 25k GitHub stars), Docmost, ix.dev (went straight into YC), Gigacatalyst. Weekly 1:1s with Julian Weisser, ODF co-founder.
programmes.brand_value: Emerging but sharp. Not a household name, but the best-positioned programme in this lane for this founder's exact shape.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Solo-only. The entire thesis: 'Most people think solo founding is just co-founding minus a co-founder. They're wrong.'
programmes.location_requirement: Three months in San Francisco, in person; optional housing above the office.
programmes.application_effort: Not verified — form not opened. Budget 2-4 hours; a launch video on the page suggests a video-forward culture.
programmes.notes: TOP PICK FOR THIS LANE. A DIFFERENT programme from ODF/On Deck Founder Fellowship despite sharing the ODF lineage, so it collides with nothing already filed. The solo-founder framing removes the most common objection this founder will hit. Money moves post-selection, so an entity is needed then, not to apply. Verify equity terms against the form.

programmes.name: ODF Founder Fellowship (ODF28)
programmes.organisation: ODF / nZero Labs, Inc. (formerly On Deck)
programmes.page_evidence: Admissions page ends with 'APPLY NOW →' and states 'ODF28 kicks off in Q3 2026 in San Francisco' and 'Interviews will be held in Q3 2026'.
programmes.cohort_dates: ODF28 kicks off Q3 2026 in San Francisco; one-week in-person onboarding sprint (five business days).
programmes.cash: None. Non-dilutive.
programmes.terms_dilution: No equity taken. Pay-what-you-can, suggested $1,000 USD, covering venue, food and year-round community infrastructure.
programmes.credits_and_tools: >$800k in perks quoted on the page (AWS, Stripe Atlas, Mercury, Carta and others).
programmes.customer_access: Not offered directly. Page notes ODF is 'most valuable if you plan to sell to US customers'.
programmes.network_quality: Strong and the main product: lifetime access to a 3,000+ member community, 80-100 builders per cohort, >50% technical. Alumni have raised >$2B; named companies include Levels, Settle, Finch, Loyal, Grow Therapy, Traba, Puzzle.
programmes.brand_value: High in US founder circles. On Deck's brand took damage in the 2022-23 contraction, but ODF spun out and the fellowship still carries weight.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Effectively solo-preferred. The 'Not a fit' list includes 'You already have a team' — designed for pre-team founders.
programmes.location_requirement: Must attend the full five-business-day SF sprint. 'We welcome applicants worldwide... Visa letters available for the onboarding week.'
programmes.application_effort: Application, optional async video, interview, optional second interview, decision in ~36 hours. Budget 2-3 hours plus a short video.
programmes.notes: Two soft frictions from the page's own 'Not a fit' list: 'Your main customer base will remain outside the US' and 'You've already raised beyond pre-seed / found product-market fit'. Neither is a wall here (zero external users, zero revenue, US-primary destination) but the US-customer point should be answered head-on. Same organisation as the Solo Founders Program — apply to both, they are distinct.

programmes.name: SPC Member Residency
programmes.region: United States (San Francisco, New York City) and India (Bangalore)
programmes.page_evidence: The /apply page returned only a single-page-app shell in my fetch — nav links (Residency, Companies, Writing) and a 'Stay in the Loop' newsletter box, no form markup. The /residency page loads and describes the programme fully but carries no 'applications open' or 'applications closed' wording. I could not confirm the form accepts input.
programmes.cohort_dates: Member Residency runs 6 months; no fixed cohort dates found on the page.
programmes.cash: None for Member Residency. The $1M cheque belongs to the Founder Fellowship, which this founder already applied to and was rejected from on 2026-08-11.
programmes.terms_dilution: Not stated on the residency page. Membership rather than investment.
programmes.network_quality: Very high. Over 1,000 technologists in a decade. Named alumni: Scott Wu (Cognition), Tuhin Srivastava (Baseten), Amit Jain (Luma AI), Anurag Goel (Render), Waseem Daher (Pilot), Feross Aboukhadijeh (Socket), Tanay Kothari (Wispr).
programmes.brand_value: Very high, and specifically respected for the -1 to 0 phase rather than growth.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Explicitly built for individuals, not teams: 'open to technologists who may or may not know they want to start a company'.
programmes.location_requirement: 'Members are expected to come into SPC throughout the week', meaning SF, NYC or Bangalore. Bangalore is where this founder already is.
programmes.application_effort: Not verified. Historically a written application then interview, with a 1-3 week response.
programmes.notes: This is the DIFFERENT SPC programme the brief asked for. The Founder Fellowship rejection on 2026-08-11 does not automatically bar a Residency application, but the same reviewers may see it — check whether SPC treats a recent rejection as a cooling-off period before spending effort. The Bangalore hub is a genuine advantage: no relocation needed.

programmes.name: Emergent Ventures (including the India vertical)
programmes.organisation: Mercatus Center, George Mason University (Tyler Cowen)
programmes.region: Global, with a dedicated India track
programmes.page_evidence: Programme page states 'Grants are awarded to thinkers and doers around the world, with dedicated support available for projects with a focus on India, Africa and the Caribbean, or Ukraine. Applicants with a specific geographic focus should select the appropriate region from a drop-down menu on the application form.' The EV India 18th cohort was announced August 2026, confirming a live pipeline.
programmes.cohort_dates: Rolling. Cohorts announced retrospectively on Marginal Revolution; EV India reached its 18th cohort in August 2026.
programmes.cash: Grant sizes are NOT published on the programme page. Third-party listings cite roughly $1k-$50k — do not quote until the form or an award announcement confirms it.
programmes.terms_dilution: Non-dilutive grant. No equity, no repayment.
programmes.network_quality: High-signal but loose: an alumni network of unusual people rather than a structured cohort. Carries real intellectual prestige and Tyler Cowen's personal attention.
programmes.brand_value: High among a specific and influential audience. An EV grant is a credible third-party signal on a deck.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Individual-first by design. Grants go to people, not companies.
programmes.location_requirement: None. Fully remote, global.
programmes.application_effort: Low. 'Applicants write a simple, short application that outlines their plan, gives some basic biographical information and a ballpark budget.' Budget 1-2 hours. No video, no references.
programmes.notes: STRONGEST EFFORT-TO-VALUE RATIO IN THIS LANE. No entity, no relocation, no dilution, ~1 hour of work. The India vertical makes the Bangalore base an asset, and critically EV India is a PERSONAL grant with no DPIIT recognition requirement, so it sidesteps the Indian-entity constraint entirely. Framing needs care: EV funds 'zero to one' ideas that improve society, so lead with the forecast-at-decision-time mechanism as an epistemics contribution, not SaaS positioning.

programmes.name: Founders, Inc. Campus
programmes.page_evidence: Apply page states: 'This is an application to join our campus for two weeks, where we'll get to know you and consider you for investment. We review applications on a rolling basis.'
programmes.cohort_dates: Rolling. Two-week campus trial, then a decision. Site says 'We'll get back to you within a month.'
programmes.cash: Site meta description states '100-250k in first checks'.
programmes.terms_dilution: Equity terms not stated on the page. Third-party listings cite 4-10%; do not quote until confirmed.
programmes.network_quality: Strong builder density: 42,000 sq ft at Fort Mason. Portfolio includes LiveKit, Rork, Paraform, Inference, Anara, Sync Labs, thirdweb.
programmes.brand_value: Moderate-to-high with SF builders, lower with institutional investors. The real value is the room, not the logo.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: No stated preference. Framing is individual-centric: 'It doesn't matter what you're building. What matters is that you're building.'
programmes.location_requirement: Two weeks on campus in San Francisco as part of the application process itself.
programmes.application_effort: Low to apply (short form). The real cost is the two-week in-person campus visit, requiring travel from Bangalore and US entry.
programmes.notes: The two-week trial IS the application — unusual and expensive in travel terms, but it favours a finished product: a reviewer can be walked through the whole Supaprod loop in person rather than reading about it. Sequence behind cheaper applications unless a US trip is already planned.

programmes.name: Entrepreneur First XF2 — Experienced Founders Program, London
programmes.page_evidence: Apply portal lists 'XF2: Experienced Founders Program in London | Fall 2026 — Start: Fall 2026. Register here if you have 7+ years experience and have either founded a startup before or been a key part of its inception.'
programmes.cohort_dates: Fall 2026, London. Exact start date not given on the portal.
programmes.cash: Not stated for XF2 on the portal. EF's standard model invests after the team-formation phase.
programmes.terms_dilution: Not stated on the portal for XF2.
programmes.network_quality: High. EF is the largest talent-investor network globally, with cohorts in London, Paris, Bangalore and San Francisco.
programmes.brand_value: High in Europe, moderate in the US.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Explicitly solo. 'EF assesses all applicants as individuals, before they have a business, cofounder or an idea.' Portal FAQ confirms 'you do not need a cofounder'.
programmes.location_requirement: 'The programs below are full-time and in person.' Relocation to London required; remote-only is not an option. EF states it will help secure a visa for applicants based outside its sites.
programmes.application_effort: Roughly a 10-12 question form, then three interview rounds, decided in 4-8 weeks. Budget 3-5 hours across the process.
programmes.notes: XF2 is the right EF door for this founder rather than the standard track: the 7+ years bar is comfortably met (ISRO, Infineon, Intellect) and Supaprod satisfies 'been a key part of its inception'. Honest caveat: EF's core proposition is co-founder matching, a poor fit for someone who has shipped 5,172 commits solo — the real pitch is London ecosystem access and the visa route.

programmes.name: Entrepreneur First Bangalore Program
programmes.page_evidence: Apply portal lists under 'BASED IN INDIA?': 'Bangalore Program — Start your journey in Bangalore. After 14 weeks, move to San Francisco for the last 3 months of the program.'
programmes.cohort_dates: Fall 2026 Bangalore cohort. 14 weeks in Bangalore, then 3 months in San Francisco.
programmes.cash: Not stated on the portal. Indian listings cite up to ₹2.25 Cr; unverified against EF's own page.
programmes.terms_dilution: Not stated on the portal.
programmes.network_quality: High. Bangalore is one of EF's four global sites.
programmes.brand_value: High in India and Europe.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Explicitly solo — same individual-first assessment as all EF programmes.
programmes.location_requirement: In person in Bangalore for 14 weeks (where the founder already is), then relocation to San Francisco for 3 months.
programmes.application_effort: Same 10-12 question form and three interview rounds as other EF tracks.
programmes.notes: The Bangalore-then-SF structure matches this founder's geography exactly: no immediate relocation, built-in US bridge. IMPORTANT UNVERIFIED RISK: check whether EF Bangalore requires an Indian entity when investment lands. That collides directly with the founder's ruling against incorporating in India. Resolve before the interview stage, not after.

programmes.name: Edge City India 2026
programmes.page_evidence: Page states: 'How to attend? Step 1: Apply Here. Step 2: We review applications on a rolling basis and follow up with next steps. Ticketing details will follow soon.' Homepage banner reads 'NEXT EVENT ↗ EDGE INDIA OCTOBER 2026 GOA'.
programmes.cohort_dates: 11 October to 1 November 2026, three-week popup village, Mandrem, North Goa.
programmes.cash: None to attendees. Edge City states it has allocated $2.5m in grants to builders across all villages via separate residencies and fellowships.
programmes.terms_dilution: None. Attendance is paid by the participant; ticketing details not yet published.
programmes.customer_access: Real. Three weeks of co-located deep work with founders, researchers and investors, plus demo days.
programmes.network_quality: High and unusual. Nine popup villages since 2023, 12,000+ builders, 100+ countries, 300+ startups and projects. Runs focused programmes on AI, crypto, longevity, governance.
programmes.brand_value: Moderate. Strong in frontier-tech and network-state circles; near-zero with conventional enterprise buyers.
programmes.location_requirement: Goa, India, up to three weeks. No international travel needed from Bangalore.
programmes.application_effort: Low. Attendance application only. Budget under an hour.
programmes.notes: Cheapest high-density network access on this list for a Bangalore-based founder — a domestic flight, no visa, no equity. Value is access and serendipity, not money. Worth pairing with a funded Edge City residency if one opens for the India village.

programmes.name: Village Global Velocity
programmes.page_evidence: Apply page states: 'Apply below to be considered for Village Global's Velocity program for early-stage founders.'
programmes.cohort_dates: Not stated on the apply page.
programmes.cash: Not stated for Velocity. The predecessor Network Catalyst offered $150,000 — do not quote that for Velocity without confirmation.

programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not stated. Village Global describes investing in 'relentlessly resourceful founders' with no published team-size rule.
programmes.location_requirement: Not stated on the apply page. Historically remote-friendly with US-centric programming.
programmes.application_effort: Single online form. Budget 1-2 hours.
programmes.notes: NAME CHANGE CAUGHT IN THIS SWEEP: the old 'Network Catalyst' URL now redirects to general fund content, and the live apply page is for a programme called 'Velocity'. Any research citing Network Catalyst terms is stale. Treat cheque size and dilution as unknown until the form states them.

programmes.name: Z Fellows
programmes.region: United States (San Francisco / New York), mostly virtual
programmes.page_evidence: Homepage describes the programme in the present tense and invites applicants: 'Z Fellows are technical builders of all ages working on side projects and startups. We are your first believer.' Caveat: the /apply path returned CRAWL_NOT_FOUND in my fetch, so the exact form URL is unconfirmed — the apply link is reached from the homepage.
programmes.cohort_dates: One-week cohorts multiple times a year, mostly virtual with the final day in person in SF or NYC.
programmes.cash: $10,000, described in third-party sources as an optional investment at a $1B valuation cap. Not confirmed on the programme page.
programmes.terms_dilution: Roughly 1% at a $1B cap per third-party sources; unverified against the programme's own page.
programmes.network_quality: Exceptional relative to cheque size. Mentors listed on the page: Marc Randolph, Naval Ravikant, Dylan Field, Guillermo Rauch, Eric Glyman, Keith Rabois, Stanley Tang, Trae Stephens, Lucy Guo, Walden Yan. Alumni include Cursor, Cognition, Etched, Mach, Whop, Mintlify, Greptile.
programmes.brand_value: Moderate-to-high and rising fast, especially via the Cursor and Cognition association.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Explicitly fine: 'you can apply solo or with your co-founders.'
programmes.location_requirement: Mostly virtual; final day in person in SF or NYC. Low relocation burden.
programmes.application_effort: Reported as ten required 100-word essays. Budget 3-4 hours. No video or references reported.
programmes.notes: The page skews heavily toward young builders ('high school dropouts, college students'), which is a positioning risk for a founder with an ISRO-to-Infineon-to-Intellect arc — but not an eligibility wall, since the page itself says 'technical builders of all ages'. The 100-word essay format rewards a single crisp mechanism claim, which suits the forecast-at-decision-time story well.

programmes.name: UK Global Entrepreneur Programme (GEP)
programmes.organisation: UK Department for Business and Trade (DBT)
programmes.region: United Kingdom (relocation of HQ or R&D presence)
programmes.page_evidence: Government page states: 'The GEP is the UK government's highly selective programme for ambitious international scaleups looking to establish a UK headquarters or R&D presence' and 'Discover how the Global Entrepreneur Programme (GEP) works and what we look for.' No closure notice appears.
programmes.cohort_dates: Rolling; no cohorts. Dealmaker-led, continuous onboarding.
programmes.cash: None. The programme is free to participants.
programmes.terms_dilution: None. No equity taken.
programmes.customer_access: Access to UK trade opportunities and strategic connections via GEP dealmakers.
programmes.network_quality: Ten 'Dealmakers' — global entrepreneurs providing continuous 1:1 mentorship. 1,400+ founders attracted since 2005; GEP companies have raised over £2.5bn and created 10,000+ jobs.
programmes.brand_value: High as a credibility and immigration signal; low as a startup-scene brand.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not stated. The programme evaluates the business and its mobility, not team size.
programmes.location_requirement: Must intend to establish a UK HQ or R&D presence. Provides endorsement under the Innovator Founder Visa, giving three years' leave to remain.
programmes.application_effort: Not verified — entry is via a qualification conversation rather than a public form. Budget a discovery call plus supporting materials.
programmes.notes: MOST RELEVANT NON-US RELOCATION LEVER FOUND. The prior session flagged an endorsement deadline as live; GEP is a second, independent endorsement route (Innovator Founder Visa) that does not depend on any accelerator decision. Two eligibility points to check against stage: the page says the business should be 'beyond the proof-of-concept stage' and must not already have a UK presence. A walkable end-to-end login is the strongest evidence against the proof-of-concept objection; zero external users is the weakest. Verify how DBT reads 'scaleup' at pre-revenue before investing effort.

programmes.name: Founder Institute — FI Core
programmes.region: Global, 200+ cities including Bangalore, Berlin, London
programmes.page_evidence: I did not load fi.co/apply or fi.co/admissions directly in this sweep. Search results indicate 'Applications for the Fall 2026 Cohort are open' on a chapter page (founderinstitute.berlin), but that is a chapter listing rather than the application form, and per the binding rules a listing is a rumour until the form contradicts it.
programmes.cohort_dates: 14-week part-time programme, chapter-dependent. Fall 2026 cohorts indicated but unverified.
programmes.cash: None. FI does not write a cheque.
programmes.terms_dilution: FI takes equity via a warrant and charges a course fee. Exact terms vary by chapter and were not verified.
programmes.network_quality: Broad rather than deep. 9,000+ graduates, chapters in 100 countries, large mentor pool of variable quality.
programmes.brand_value: Low to moderate. Little signalling value with top-tier investors and sometimes read negatively.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Explicitly built for solo, idea-stage founders — FI's core audience is pre-team.
programmes.location_requirement: Chapter-based and part-time; a Bangalore or virtual chapter would require no relocation.
programmes.application_effort: Low. Online form plus an aptitude assessment. Budget 1-2 hours.
programmes.notes: Included for completeness, not recommended. A founder with 5,172 commits and a working end-to-end product is well past FI's idea-stage curriculum, and the fee-plus-warrant structure buys little he does not already have. Rank near the bottom of this lane.

programmes.terms_dilution: Reported as 0% immediate dilution via uncapped SAFE. Unverified.

programmes.network_quality: Reported as strong: weekly dinners with founders of Ramp, Cognition, Mercor, Deel, Kalshi. Office space in SF or NY.

programmes.application_effort: Unverified.
programmes.notes: High potential value if the remote-plus-customer-intros combination holds, because it addresses the two things Supaprod most needs (US network reach, first external users) without relocation. programmes.name: Unshackled Ventures
programmes.page_evidence: Site header and hero both carry an active 'Pitch Us' / 'Pitch Us Now' call to action linking to the application, with the positioning 'We back bold technical founders with capital, immigration support, and conviction — pre-product, pre-revenue, pre-visa.'
programmes.cohort_dates: Rolling. Not a cohort programme.
programmes.cash: Inception-stage first cheque; size not stated on the page.
programmes.terms_dilution: Equity investment. Terms not published.
programmes.network_quality: 80 companies, 200+ entrepreneurs. Runs 'U-Labs' and a 'Network' programme listed in site nav.
programmes.brand_value: Moderate generally, high specifically among immigrant founders.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not stated. The requirement is that at least one founder is an immigrant.
programmes.location_requirement: US-bound. The whole thesis is starting companies in the US.
programmes.application_effort: Single pitch form. Budget 1-2 hours plus a deck.

For an Indian national targeting the US, that service is arguably worth more than the money. Note the pitch form is hosted on a Lovable app subdomain — confirm it is genuinely theirs before submitting anything sensitive.

programmes.name: Slush 100 (and Slush 2026 startup programme)
programmes.page_evidence: Slush startups page states: 'Slush 100 – €500,000 equity free. The largest equity-free amount in a startup competition, ever... Learn more and apply.' The dedicated explore.slush.org/startups/slush-100/ page returned HTTP 525 in my fetch, so the specific deadline could not be read.
programmes.cohort_dates: Slush 2026 is 18-19 November 2026 in Helsinki, with Day 0 for Founders on 17 November.
programmes.cash: €500,000 equity-free to the Slush 100 winner, per the Slush startups page. An older source cites €1,000,000 in equity funding from General Catalyst and Cherry — the current page says €500,000 equity free, so use that.
programmes.terms_dilution: Equity-free prize. 'no strings attached, no reporting burden, no ties'.
programmes.customer_access: 20,000+ meetings, investor office hours, matchmaking sprint, startup stage and booths.
programmes.network_quality: Europe's highest-density founder-investor event. '$4T AUM. One VC for every two founders.'
programmes.brand_value: Very high in Europe. Making the Slush 100 shortlist is a real credential.
programmes.location_requirement: Attendance in Helsinki required for the competition. Startup ticket €395.

programmes.notes: ENTITY FLAG: reported Slush 100 eligibility is 'incorporated during or after 2021 and has raised less than €2M', which implies an incorporated company is needed to ENTER. That is a genuine pre-submission entity requirement if confirmed — the one condition on this list that no-entity does not survive, so verify it on the form. Attending Slush itself requires only a ticket, not an entity, and remains valuable independently.

programmes.region: Global (hubs in San Francisco and Berlin)
programmes.page_evidence: The page's primary call to action reads 'Apply for the 2028 cohort' alongside 'Submit a nomination'. The 2027 cycle deadline of 31 July 2026 has passed; the page now points at the next cohort.

programmes.solo_founder_stance: Individual fellowship — solo is the default unit.

Low priority; listed so it is not rediscovered later.

programmes.cash: None directly. Fellows get access to grant programmes for personal projects.
programmes.terms_dilution: None.
programmes.network_quality: Small, high-trust community of technologists, running since 2012 and led by former Fellows.
programmes.brand_value: Moderate and specific.
programmes.location_requirement: Retreat attendance, fully sponsored.
programmes.hard_blocker: Age. 'The only requirement is that Fellowship applicants are between the ages of 18 and 23 at the time of application, with rare exceptions for 24-year-olds.' This founder's career arc (ISRO, then Infineon, then Intellect) places him well outside that band. A published eligibility wall, not a preference.
programmes.application_effort: Not applicable.
programmes.notes: Named in the brief and checked properly rather than assumed. Two independent reasons to drop: the age wall is real and published, and applications are not open. Recommend removing from future sweeps of this lane.

programmes.name: StartX

'A Stanford-affiliated founder is someone who was/is a Stanford alumni, undergraduate student, graduate student, faculty member, post doctoral scholar, academic staff member, or fellow in a recognized Stanford fellowship program.' programmes.name: Hampton
programmes.region: United States and international chapter cities
programmes.page_evidence: FAQ page states 'Anyone can feel free to apply through this application' and describes a live four-step vetting process ending in an invite.
programmes.cohort_dates: None. Continuous membership with monthly Core group meetings.
programmes.cash: None. Costs $8,500 per year.
programmes.terms_dilution: None. Membership dues only.
programmes.customer_access: 1,000+ operating founders and CEOs — a plausible buyer pool, but at a price.
programmes.network_quality: High trust and well curated: moderated Core groups of nine founders, city chapters, and a member veto step that keeps quality up.
programmes.brand_value: Moderate. Reads as an operator community rather than a startup credential.
programmes.location_requirement: 'You must live within one of our Chapter Cities.'
programmes.hard_blocker: Revenue or funding threshold. 'Your current business(es) must be generating >$3M in revenue, OR you must have raised >$3M in venture capital, OR you must have had a previously successful exit (>$10M).' With zero revenue and no raise, none of the three is met. The first screen explicitly checks 'Is your company doing at least $3M in revenue?'
programmes.application_effort: Application, interview, community veto, founder sign-off.
programmes.notes: Genuinely blocked today on a published, quantitative threshold — one of the few rows where the wall is arithmetic rather than judgement. Revisit only after a raise above $3M. Listed so it is not re-researched.

programmes.name: GitHub Accelerator
programmes.page_evidence: The page's own heading still reads 'GitHub Accelerator 2024' and its only calls to action are 'Meet the selected projects' and 'Sign up for updates'. There is no application form and no statement that applications are closed — so the programme appears dormant rather than explicitly shut.
programmes.cohort_dates: 10-week peer cohort, 5-10 hours of instruction. Last confirmed cohort 2024.
programmes.cash: Funding provided; amount not stated on the current page.
programmes.terms_dilution: Non-dilutive sponsorship of open-source maintainers.

programmes.brand_value: High within open source.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Individual maintainers and teams up to three welcome.
programmes.location_requirement: None. Virtual.
programmes.hard_blocker: Licensing model. Eligibility requires being 'a current contributor or maintainer of an open source project on GitHub' with 'an open source license and community'. Supaprod is a closed, private-beta commercial product, so it does not qualify as it stands.
programmes.application_effort: Not applicable.
programmes.notes: Two independent problems: the programme looks dormant since 2024, and Supaprod is not open source. Only becomes relevant if a genuine component of the stack is ever open-sourced — a product decision, not an application decision. Do not pursue.

programmes.name: Contrary Sabbatical
programmes.page_evidence: Both applications.contrary.com and applications.contrary.com/apply-sabbatical failed to load for me (fetch errors on two separate tools, and WebFetch returned no content at all). Every substantive detail I could find dates from the 2022 programme announcement, so I cannot tell whether Sabbatical still runs.
programmes.cohort_dates: Historically a one-year full-focus commitment. Current cycle unknown.
programmes.cash: Historically up to $250,000 across up to 5 founders per cycle. 2022 figures, unverified for 2026.
programmes.terms_dilution: Equity investment; terms not verified.
programmes.network_quality: Calls with the Contrary investing team, hiring network access, introductions to operators who have scaled companies to thousands of employees, and office space depending on city.
programmes.brand_value: Moderate and rising.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Historically stated as open to anyone regardless of age or location, with the only requirement being a full year of focus.
programmes.location_requirement: None stated historically; office space offered depending on city.
programmes.application_effort: Historically an email to sabbatical@contrary.com plus a form. Unverified.
programmes.notes: Distinguish carefully from Contrary's other two programmes, both walled: the Venture Partner programme requires enrolment at a US or Canadian university, and the Research Fellowship is a paid writing gig, not a founder programme. Sabbatical is the only Contrary door open to a non-student founder, and its 'quit your job and go all in' framing matches this founder's situation — but the page would not load, so phase 2 must confirm it still exists before any effort.

programmes.name: Global Entrepreneur in Residence (GEIR)
programmes.organisation: Multiple US universities (Babson, UC San Diego, NJIT, William Paterson, UMass)
programmes.region: United States (Massachusetts, New Jersey, California, Ohio)
programmes.page_evidence: I did not load any GEIR programme page directly. Search summaries cite a Babson application cycle closing 1 December 2026 and describe NJIT, UC San Diego and William Paterson programmes, but neither the form state nor the exact eligibility text was confirmed on a programme page.
programmes.cohort_dates: Varies by university. Cap-exempt H-1B petitions can be filed at any time of year rather than only in the annual lottery.
programmes.cash: None. A part-time university salary funds the visa position.
programmes.terms_dilution: None. No equity.
programmes.network_quality: University-dependent; generally regional rather than national.
programmes.brand_value: Low as a startup credential; high as an immigration mechanism.
programmes.location_requirement: Relocation to the sponsoring university's state, with a minimum of 8 hours per week on campus.
programmes.hard_blocker: Probable but NOT confirmed. Search summaries describe participants as 'typically current or recently graduated international students' at the sponsoring US institution and 'international students eligible for cap-exempt H-1B visa status'. A TUM alumnus with no US student history likely fails this, but the requirement varies by university and I could not confirm it from a programme page — so I am deliberately not calling it a definite wall.
programmes.application_effort: Unverified. Varies by university.
programmes.notes: Included because it is the cheapest known route to a US work visa that does not depend on winning an accelerator, which matters given the endorsement timing pressure from the prior session. The single question phase 2 must answer is whether any GEIR site accepts a non-US-educated applicant. If even one does, this becomes materially more valuable than several better-known programmes on this list.
